title: Perimeter, Area and Volume
seo_title: Grade 5 Perimeter, Area and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Measure perimeter using rulers or measuring tapes; find areas of regular and irregular shapes by counting squares on grids in order to develop an understanding of square units; find volume or capacity of objects by packing or filling them, and by counting cubes in order to develop an understanding of cubic units.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 perimeter, area and volume worksheets: perimeter of polygons, area by counting squares and volume by counting cubes. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Perimeter: around. Area: inside. Volume: space taken up.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter is the distance around a shape: add all the sides.
  • Area is the space inside a shape: count the squares. A rectangle has rows × columns squares.
  • Volume is the space an object takes up: count the cubes, including hidden ones.
  • Perimeter is in cm or m; area in square units (cm²); volume in cubic units (cm³).

Examples

Example

A rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm

perimeter: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4

area: 6 × 4 squares

Answer: 20 cm and 24 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Two sides onlyAdd all four sides.
Area or perimeter?Area is inside; perimeter is around.
Visible cubes onlyCount the hidden cubes too.

items.q: Why can you multiply to find the number of squares in a rectangle?
c: The rows get longer and longer
Every row has the same number
items.e: In a rectangle, the squares sit in equal rows. Equal groups can be multiplied: number of rows × squares in each row.

items.q: Rectangle A has 4 rows of 9 squares. Rectangle B has 9 rows of 4 squares. Which is true?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36 and 9 × 4 = 36. Turning a rectangle does not change its area.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. How many unit cubes are in the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. 2 layers: 12 × 2 = 24 cubes.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 4 layers: 10 × 4 = 40 cubic units. Count the cubes you cannot see, too (only 28 cubes show a face).

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?

items.q: How many unit cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes across and 4 cubes deep: 5 × 4 = 20 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 3 = 15 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: Both rectangles have an area of 36 cm²: one is 9 cm by 4 cm, the other is 12 cm by 3 cm. Which has the longer perimeter?
items.e: 9 cm by 4 cm: 18 + 8 = 26 cm. 12 cm by 3 cm: 24 + 6 = 30 cm. The same area can have different perimeters.

items.q: Both rectangles have a perimeter of 24 m: one is 6 m by 6 m, the other is 10 m by 2 m. Which has the bigger area?
items.e: 6 × 6 = 36 m² and 10 × 2 = 20 m². The same perimeter can give very different areas.

items.q: How many different rectangles with whole-number sides have an area of 24 cm²? (A turned rectangle counts as the same one.)
items.e: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6: 4 rectangles. Their perimeters are all different: 50, 28, 22 and 20 cm. (8 counts each turned rectangle twice.)

items.q: All these rectangles have an area of 36 m². Which has the shortest perimeter?
items.e: Perimeters: 6 by 6 = 24 m, 9 by 4 = 26 m, 12 by 3 = 30 m, 36 by 1 = 74 m. For the same area, the closer the shape is to a square, the shorter the perimeter.

items.q: Refilwe has 20 m of fence for a rectangular garden. Which garden gives the most area?
items.e: All use 20 m of fence. Areas: 5 × 5 = 25 m², 6 × 4 = 24 m², 7 × 3 = 21 m², 8 × 2 = 16 m². The square gives the most area.

items.q: A rectangle is 6 cm by 4 cm. Both sides are doubled to 12 cm by 8 cm. What happens to the area?
items.e: Old area: 6 × 4 = 24 cm². New area: 12 × 8 = 96 cm². 96 ÷ 24 = 4, so it is 4 times as big. (The perimeter only doubles: 20 cm to 40 cm.)

items.q: Which rectangle has an area of 18 cm² and a perimeter of 18 cm?
items.e: 6 × 3 = 18 cm² and 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 cm. (9 by 2 has a perimeter of 22 cm; 5 by 4 and 7 by 2 have areas of 20 cm² and 14 cm².)

items.q: Ofentse makes a poster for the Terry Fox Run. It is 60 cm long and 45 cm wide. What is its area?
Fatima’s rectangular vegetable bed has an area of 96 m². It is 12 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8, so the bed is 8 m wide. (84 comes from subtracting: 96 − 12.)

items.q: The reading corner is 6 m long and 5 m wide. Each carpet tile covers 1 m². The class has put down 18 tiles. How many more tiles are needed?
items.e: Whole corner: 6 × 5 = 30 tiles. Still needed: 30 − 18 = 12 tiles. (4 uses the perimeter, 22, instead of the area.)

items.q: Mbali’s bedroom floor is 5 m by 4 m. A rug 3 m by 2 m lies on it. What area of floor is not covered?
items.e: Floor: 5 × 4 = 20 m². Rug: 3 × 2 = 6 m². 20 − 6 = 14 m². (4 m² comes from (5 − 3) × (4 − 2), which takes away from the sides instead of the areas.)

items.q: A square photo frame has a perimeter of 64 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Each side: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm. Area: 16 × 16 = 256 cm². (4 096 uses 64 as the side.)

items.q: Precious’s bedroom is 4 m by 4 m. Nomsa’s bedroom is 5 m by 3 m. Both have a perimeter of 16 m. Whose bedroom has the bigger area?
items.e: Precious: 4 × 4 = 16 m². Nomsa: 5 × 3 = 15 m². 16 − 15 = 1, so Precious’s room is bigger by 1 m². The same perimeter does not mean the same area.

items.q: Jabu has 20 m of fence for a rectangular garden. Which garden gives the most area?
